PREEMPT_RT needs to hand a special state into __schedule() when a task
blocks on a 'sleeping' spin/rwlock. This is required to handle
rcu_note_context_switch() correctly without having special casing in the
RCU code. From an RCU point of view the blocking on the sleeping spinlock
is equivalent to preemption
column2: because the task might be in a read side

column1: critical section.
schedule_debug() also has a check which would trigger with the !preempt
case
column2: but that could be handled differently.

column1: To avoid adding another argument and extra checks which cannot be optimized
out by the compiler
column2: the following solution has been chosen:

column1: - Replace the boolean 'preempt' argument with an unsigned integer
'sched_mode' argument and define constants to hand in:
(0 == no preemption
- Add two masks to apply on that mode: one for the debug/rcu invocations
and one for the actual scheduling decision.
For a non RT kernel these masks are UINT_MAX
which allows the compiler to optimize the AND operation out
not masking out anything. IOW
column2: it's not different from the boolean.

column1: RT enabled kernels will define these masks separately.
No functional change.
